summary:
MARS GUARD – Smart Navigation for Safer Mars Exploration

We developed **MARS GUARD**, an interactive web-based platform designed to support safer and smarter exploration of the Martian surface. It helps users select starting and destination locations on Mars, visualize possible travel routes, estimate distances, and explore geographical features such as terrain and elevation. The platform combines interactive mapping and web technologies to make Mars surface exploration easier to understand.
Mars has a diverse landscape consisting of craters, valleys, mountains, slopes, and other challenging geographical features. These conditions make surface navigation difficult for future astronauts and robotic explorers.
MARS GUARD addresses this challenge by providing an interactive Mars map where users can choose two locations and visualize a possible route between them. It provides distance information and helps users understand the geographical conditions along their planned journey. By bringing important surface information together in one platform, it supports better-informed route planning and exploration.
As humanity prepares for future missions to Mars, safe and efficient navigation will become increasingly important. Choosing suitable travel routes can help astronauts and robotic rovers avoid challenging geographical areas and make their exploration missions more effective.
details:
MARS GUARD – Interactive Mars Exploration and Crew Safety System

1. Project Overview

MARS GUARD is an interactive, web-based Mars exploration and crew safety planning platform developed to make Martian surface exploration more accessible and understandable. The project focuses on helping users explore the geographical landscape of Mars, identify locations, visualize possible travel routes, and estimate distances between selected destinations.

Our project uses Jezero Crater as the primary study area, providing an interactive environment for exploring the Martian surface.

2. Problem Statement

Mars has a challenging geographical environment consisting of craters, valleys, mountains, slopes, rocks, and loose soil. These surface conditions can create difficulties for future astronauts and robotic explorers travelling across the planet.

Understanding the geographical conditions and planning suitable routes are important steps towards safer and more efficient Mars exploration. However, exploring different planetary resources and interpreting geographical information can be difficult for beginners and researchers.

3. Our Solution

MARS GUARD provides a user-friendly interactive platform that brings Mars mapping and basic route-planning features together in one place. Users can explore the Martian surface, select geographical locations, draw proposed routes, and calculate approximate distances using latitude and longitude coordinates.

The platform also includes an astronaut safety checklist that highlights important factors to consider during mission planning, including terrain conditions, rocks, steep slopes, loose soil, radiation, sunlight, spacesuit mobility, and communication planning.

4. Key Features

  • Interactive Mars Map: Explore the Martian surface using NASA/JPL Mars map resources.
  • Jezero Crater Exploration: Navigate directly to the selected study area.
  • Route Visualization: Mark multiple points and draw a proposed travel route.
  • Mars Distance Calculator: Estimate surface distances between two locations using Mars's approximate mean radius.
  • Global Mars View: Explore the wider Martian landscape.
  • Astronaut Safety Checklist: Review important geographical and mission-planning considerations.
  • NASA and USGS Resources: Access planetary mapping and exploration resources.

5. Technology Used

The website is developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. Leaflet.js provides interactive mapping functionality, while NASA/JPL Mars Trek map tiles provide Martian surface visualization. A spherical-distance calculation using Mars's approximate radius is used to estimate distances between coordinates.

6. Impact and Importance

MARS GUARD demonstrates how web technologies and planetary mapping resources can support the understanding of Martian surface navigation. It provides an accessible educational platform for students, researchers, and space enthusiasts interested in planetary exploration.

Although it is an early-stage prototype and does not automatically detect hazards or identify the safest route, it establishes a foundation for future improvements such as elevation analysis, geological overlays, terrain-aware route comparison, and automated hazard assessment.

7. Our Vision

Our vision is to contribute to future human and robotic Mars exploration by developing accessible tools that make planetary navigation easier to understand and more informed.

MARS GUARD – Explore Mars Smarter. Navigate Mars Safer. Discover Beyond Earth.
